items.title: What's new, right on the board
items.text: This list. After an update a small red dot on Feedback tells you that something changed, so you never miss a new feature.

items.title: Feedback on one page
items.text: Write to us at the top, see what others asked for below. Tap "Want it" or "Don't need" to vote, tap again to take it back.

image.name: r13-feedback
image.alt: The feedback panel: a box to write to the makers, below it a table of ideas with votes

items.title: Anonymous means anonymous
items.text: In anonymous mode nobody can tell who played which card, not even with the browser's developer tools. Cards stay on the table until the next round, and you can still throw emojis at them.
items.where: Board settings → Results → Names on revealed cards

items.title: Play via your AI assistant (beta)
items.text: Your assistant (Claude, ChatGPT …) can take your seat: it sees the board, plays the card you name and tells you what happens at the table.

image.name: r10-ai
image.alt: The dialog "Play via your AI assistant" with the connector URL and three short steps

items.title: You see who plays via AI
items.text: A small robot next to a name shows that an AI assistant sits there for that person. Your team can switch AI assistants off.
items.where: Board settings → Team → Allow AI assistants

items.title: Connect your tools
items.text: With an API key, Jira or your own scripts can set the note and fill the item list for you – no more copy and paste before the session.

image.name: r9-apikeys
image.alt: The section "API keys" in the You menu with a field for the key's name and the button "Create key"

items.title: A tidier You menu
items.text: Name, role, appearance and your data in one calm place. "Delete my data" removes everything about you in one go.

items.title: Taken off the table? Still watching
items.text: Whoever was removed from the table now simply watches as an observer and can join again with one click.
items.where: the observer line below the table

items.title: A faster start
items.text: The board shows up sooner, especially on slow connections.
items.where: every time you open a board

items.title: Light stays light
items.text: The board opens straight in your colour mode – no dark flash before the light page appears.
items.where: You → Appearance, or the moon/sun button

items.title: Every emoji once a day
items.text: Each emoji can be thrown once per day and person – the bar shows what you have left. So you think twice where it lands, and fish storms are over. Nudging is not counted.
items.where: tap a card on the table

image.name: r5-emoji
image.alt: The emoji bar above a card on the table, with the number of throws left below each emoji

items.title: A list of items to estimate
items.text: Put your backlog items in a list, estimate one after the other and close each with its value. When you are done, copy the results or download them as CSV.

image.name: r4-items
image.alt: The topic panel with the tab Items: a list of items, the first one active

items.title: The median next to the average
items.text: After the reveal a line marks the median as well – handy when one card is far off.
items.where: Board settings → Results → Average and median

items.title: The timer starts by itself
items.text: Let the timer start with every new round or with every new item.

items.title: You hear a nudge
items.text: A soft sound and a hint in the browser tab when someone nudges you, so you notice it even in another tab.
items.where: You → Play a sound when someone nudges you

items.title: Fold the sidebar away
items.text: On a computer you can collapse the column on the right to a narrow strip or drag it wider. The board remembers your choice for voting and for results.
items.where: the arrows at the top of the sidebar

image.name: r31-rail
image.alt: The board with the sidebar collapsed to a narrow strip on the right edge

items.title: New cards
items.text: Crisp cards in a hand-drawn style on every screen, with the name right above each card.

image.name: r3-table
image.alt: Revealed cards on the table with the names above them

items.title: A deck for every question
items.text: Pick from groups of decks: estimates (Fibonacci, T-shirt sizes …), traffic lights, team assessment, mood and more – or make your own set with your own values.

image.name: r3-decks
image.alt: The deck settings with groups of card decks

items.title: Throw, nudge, remove
items.text: Tap a card on the table to throw an emoji at it, nudge someone who is still thinking, or take someone off the table who has left.
items.where: tap a card on the table

items.title: See changed cards
items.text: If someone changes their card after the reveal, the first card stays visible underneath.

items.title: Timer with a timebox
items.text: Choose 3, 5 or 10 minutes (or your own) and everybody sees the same countdown – or simply run a stopwatch.

image.name: r2-timer
image.alt: The timer panel with mode, timebox and auto-start

items.title: New round where your hand is
items.text: The button for a new round sits at the bottom right, next to the timer.

items.title: Tips for your round
items.text: Short tips next to the table explain the deck in play. Know it all already? Switch them off for the team.

items.title: Swipe through your cards
items.text: On phones and tablets your cards are a carousel: swipe and tap the one in the middle.

items.title: Back in sync after a break
items.text: If your laptop slept or the network dropped, the board reconnects on its own and tells you while it does.

items.title: A fresh look, the same game
items.text: A calmer board with clear places for the topic, the table and your cards. Everything works as before, it just reads easier – in light and in dark.

image.name: r1-board
image.alt: The whole board: header, the table with cards, the sidebar and the deck at the bottom

items.title: Menus that keep the table in view
items.text: Settings open as a panel next to the table on a computer and as a sheet from the bottom on a phone.

items.title: Cards that fit your screen
items.text: Cards grow and shrink with your window, so a big team fits on a laptop and on a phone.

items.title: Ideas & bugs
items.text: Tell us what you need and vote on what others asked for, right from the board.
